Hi Alex / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Neubula's team has been running a pilot on the sandbox credits you provided and the usage numbers are encouraging — attaching a short usage report. We're discussing converting part of the sandbox pool to a small committed reserved capacity (Q3 pilot -> Q4 committed). A couple of procurement questions popped up that I wanted to confirm before I loop in our legal/procurement team: 

- Can promotional sandbox credits be converted to reserved capacity credits? If so, do they carry any restrictions (proration, vesting, time window)?
- Is there any circumstance where Redwood would claw back or "rollback" promotional credits after conversion (we want to avoid surprise post-signature reversals)?
- Will a conversion trigger any minimum usage floor or early-termination charge?

High-level ask: if you can share the simplest conversion path (example numbers) and any standard language we should expect in the SOW/appendix, that will help me prepare procurement.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Hi Julia — great to hear the pilot is performing well. I pulled together a quick summary below and attached the deck we ran through. TL;DR: yes, we support a clean conversion path; we just ask for a short conversion window and a modest usage-floor during the initial committed term.

Conversion summary (example):
- Sandbox promo credits convertible up to 50% of total pilot consumption into committed credit offset (one-time conversion during a 90-day window after pilot end).
- Converted credits apply as a prepayment against the first 3 months of the committed monthly invoice (prorated if smaller than first-month consumption).
- Vesting: converted promo credit discount phases out linearly over the first 6 months of the committed term (this is to avoid an economic cliff and to align incentives).

Rollback / clawback scenarios (what triggers a reversal):
- Abuse/fraud: if usage patterns show automated abuse or repeated policy violations, we reserve the right to void conversions (rare; we will provide evidence and a remediation window).
- Significant metric changes: material change in account ownership or transfer of data outside of agreed boundaries could trigger review.

Usage floor & termination:
- We do commonly include a nominal monthly committed-usage floor (e.g., 30% of agreed monthly tokens) for the first 6 months to stabilize unit economics.
- Early termination: standard termination fees apply only if the committed capacity is canceled within the first 3 months (pro-rated refund of remaining converted-credit value is possible in defined cases).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben will draft a short conversion-term appendix that can sit behind the SOW (sample attached).
2) If that looks OK to you, we can circulate a redline for procurement + legal.
3) We can add a one-paragraph "no-sneaky-clawback" sentence to reduce procurement friction.

Attaching: Redwood_Demo_Slides.pdf

Would you be free for a 20-min sync tomorrow to confirm numbers?

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Alex. Julia — appreciate the clear ask. Quick clarifications from our side before we push to legal: 

- Discount stacking: promotional credits converted to committed credits do not stack with other percentage discounts in the first billing cycle (we'll show the net effective rate in the appendix).
- Early-conversion bonus: we're prepared to offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the converted value if Neubula signs the committed term within 30 days of the conversion window close.
- Accounting friendliness: we'd prefer the appendix to show the converted-credit as an invoice credit line item (helps finance).

I've attached a draft conversion-term-draft.pdf that maps the example numbers and includes a short "non-clawback except for fraud" clause that is intentionally narrow. Please review.

Julia — if procurement needs SOC2 or audit artifacts, Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate collecting the pack. Also linking the HubSpot deal here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345RW-2467 — I added a mutual action plan card (MAP) with milestones we can share with your procurement.
